title: One Required Swap to Match
statement:
You get two strings s and target of lowercase letters. You must make exactly one swap in s: pick two different positions i ≠ j and exchange their letters.

Return true if some such swap turns s into target. Note that the swap is required, even when s already equals target.

examples.why: Swap positions 1 and 2: r and a trade places.
The strings already match, but a swap is required, and every swap of two different letters breaks the match.
Swapping the two e's changes nothing, so the strings still match after the required swap.

constraints: Both strings have only lowercase English letters
hints: Compare the strings position by position. How many positions may differ for the answer to be true?
If two positions differ, they must be mirror images: s[i] = target[j] and s[j] = target[i]. What if no positions differ?
With zero differences you still have to swap something. That only works if some letter appears twice in s.

explain.intuition:
A swap changes at most two positions. So collect the positions where s and target differ. If there are exactly two, say i and j, swapping them works only when the letters are crossed: s[i] = target[j] and s[j] = target[i]. Any other count of differences, except zero, means false.

Zero differences is the trap. The swap is mandatory, so you need a swap that changes nothing: two equal letters. A set of seen letters finds a repeat in one pass.
steps: If the strings are equal, return whether any letter appears at least twice in s.
Otherwise collect the indexes where they differ. Return false unless there are exactly two.
Return whether the two differing letters are crossed.
pitfalls: Returning true when the strings are already equal. Without a duplicate letter, the required swap breaks them.
Checking only that exactly two positions differ, without checking that the letters cross. "abc" vs "acd" differs in two places but no swap fixes it.
Forgetting that the lengths may differ.

complexity.space: O(1) (at most 26 letters in the set)

solutions.title: Try every swap
solutions.idea: Swap each pair of positions and compare with the target.

solutions.title: Count the mismatches
solutions.idea: Equal strings need a repeated letter. Otherwise exactly two mismatches whose letters cross.

followups: Allow at most k swaps. Can you still decide it in linear time?
Return the pair of indexes to swap, or [-1, -1] if none works.
